Avery / Marissa — quick internal read:

Technical take (short): yes, we can safely absorb the ~900 TPS short bursts on Hosted for the volumes stated if we apply:
- Scheduled burst reservations: we pre-allocate a burst pool in us-west for their 3 monthly windows (pre-warm on the scheduled time).
- Aggressive KV/prefix caching for user sessions to reduce token compute for repeated prefixes (we need their typical prompt reuse rates).
- Autoscaling threshold tuning + a fallback routing policy to a slightly cheaper lower-latency optimized model variant when the primary pool is saturated.

Operational caveats: sustained bursts longer than ~12 minutes or unpredictable spikes would push us to recommend Dedicated. Also, at 13M sustained monthly token upper bound with frequent high bursts, unit economics shift.

Commercial suggestion (for 12-mo commit, based on 9.5M expected):
- Option A (Hosted, committed 12-mo): $590 / 1M tokens, with 3 pre-scheduled burst reservations included per month (up to 1k TPS for 12 minutes each). Overages billed at standard hosted rate.
- Option B (Hosted + buffer credit): $520 / 1M tokens with purchase of 2 burst-credit bundles (each bundle = 30 minutes total burst at up to 1k TPS) — useful if they want a lower effective $/1M but pay for burst capacity up front.
- Option C (Dedicated recommendation): propose pricing separately if they want fully guaranteed headroom for unpredictable bursts (we should have a quick Dedicated sketch ready).

Next steps: I can draft proposed SOW language for the burst reservations and the pricing bands. Avery — if you want the numbers tighter, I’ll pull the expected unit cost at 9.5M and model out host vs dedicated delta.
